messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: BFGS Optimization
parts:
I'm about to push a bunch of changes which I will describe in a series
of emails. The work, done over the past week or so, come together to
make Stan much faster in a number of ways (any models using multI_* or
*wishart distributions should be much faster), and in particular,
greatly improves the ability to work with Gaussian Process models.

Finally...

3) BFGS Implementation

When trying to optimize a GPLVM-type model I found the Nesterov method
to have poor convergence (it very quickly stopped making significant
progress) and the Newton method to be too slow due to the need for the
Hessian. Instead I've implemented a BFGS-based quasi-Newton method
with line search (using the strong Wolfe conditions, for anyone
keeping score). The implementation should be fairly robust and for
people looking to use point estimates (*ducking Andrews glare*) I
would recommend this be the default, first-try method. Right now it
is available with --point_estimate_bfgs.

This is not quite the ideal optimizer in my mind, as it may become too
expensive for problems with more than ~20k parameters. L-BFGS would
be better, but I doubt I'll get to implementing that in the near
future.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.subject: Re: BFGS Optimization
parts:
On Wednesday, April 17, 2013 1:09:34 PM UTC-4, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
3) BFGS Implementation

When trying to optimize a GPLVM-type model I found the Nesterov method
to have poor convergence (it very quickly stopped making significant
progress) and the Newton method to be too slow due to the need for the
Hessian.  Instead I've implemented a BFGS-based quasi-Newton method
with line search (using the strong Wolfe conditions, for anyone
keeping score).  The implementation should be fairly robust and for
people looking to use point estimates (*ducking Andrews glare*) I
would recommend this be the default, first-try method.  Right now it
is available with --point_estimate_bfgs.

The strong Wolfe conditions are probably fine for the problem you had in mind, but this paper

http://people.orie.cornell.edu/aslewis/publications/bfgs_inexactLS.pdf

convinced me that the weak Wolfe conditions were a better default since the software can't know how well-behaved the user's objective function will be. Can you expose the BFGSOptions() and add a flag for strong / weak Wolfe conditions? I'll implement the weak version of the algorithm (which is super easy) if you don't want to.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] BFGS Optimization
parts:
On 4/17/13 1:09 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> I'm about to push a bunch of changes which I will describe in a series
> of emails.

...

Testing: talk to Daniel.


Doc: I'll add the function docs.

Adding GP example doc should be easy if I can understand
the new models.

Are you planning more changes to the optimization command-line
calls before I doc them?

I'll add some simulated data examples to illustrate
optimization.


Stan 2.0.0 commands: I think it makes most sense to break
the stan command down into subcommands like git does. So that'd
be:

stan nuts ...args for nuts3...

stan metropolis ...args for metropolis...

and to get help on Stan generally,

stan --help

and nuts in particular,

stan nuts --help

I'm not sure what the appropriate subcommands should
be for optimization methods.

Finally, I'm happy as a clam that Marcus figured out how to
re-use solver output. It's something Ben's been wanting
and I've been scratching my head over how to do
for about as long as Stan's been around. This'll also make
a nice section of the yet-to-be-written auto-diff paper
(but writing up a bunch of papers is on my short-term
to-do list).

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: BFGS Optimization
parts:
On Wednesday, April 17, 2013 1:54:40 PM UTC-4, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
I wouldn't object to someone adding an option to use the weak Wolfe
conditions, but I'd need to read over that paper carefully before I'd
suggest it as a default.

Perhaps I should have said that Overton's optimization software

http://www.cs.nyu.edu/overton/software/hanso/

uses weak Wolfe as a default, and I wasn't going to disagree with him.

I don't know of a case where weak Wolfe is insufficient for convergence, although you can get faster convergence on sufficiently well-behaved problems with strong Wolfe. But it is not too hard to construct a problem where strong Wolfe doesn't work numerically. So, that is the argument for a weak Wolfe default in a nutshell.

Ben

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: BFGS Optimization
parts:
Thanks Matt and Andrew.

With the changes I've just pushed, I would think it should be very
plausible to fit a GP with a couple hundred data points using MCMC in
Stan in a reasonable period of time.

Right now I can fit (using MAP) a GP-based latent variable model with
~2k data points using BFGS in under 30min on a 3yr old Macbook Pro.
Fitting just hyperparameters for a GP regression/classification
problem should be even faster.

That said, the performance we have right now is pretty close to
optimal for Stan for most typical GP models. There are a couple
places we could make it even faster, but I suspect they would only
shave off maybe 10% or 15% of runtime.

Cheers,
Marcus
